    reasonable_demand_mask = (cluster_demand_i <= 2.0) & (cluster_demand_j <= 2.0)
    boost_mask = intra_cluster_mask & reasonable_demand_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[boost_mask] = 0.15
    
    # Penalize inter-cluster edges connecting high-demand clusters
    inter_cluster_mask = (cluster_i != cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1) & (cluster_j != -1)
    high_demand_inter_mask = (cluster_demand_i > avg_demand) & (cluster_demand_j > avg_demand)
    penalty_mask = inter_cluster_mask & high_demand_inter_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[penalty_mask] = -0.1

    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + cluster_boost[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware component
    demand_i = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    demand_j = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    combined_demand_factor = (demand_i + demand_j) / (2 * avg_demand + 1e-8)
    capacity_adjustment = -0.05 * combined_demand_factor
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + capacity_adjustment[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware component: Consider individual demand ratios
    demand_ratio_i = demand_i / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    demand_ratio_j = demand_j / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    high_demand_connection_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_both = (demand_ratio_i > 1.0) & (demand_ratio_j > 1.0)
    high_demand_connection_penalty[high_demand_both] = -0.05
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_connection_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Depot connection adjustments
    depot_return_benefit = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    depot_exit_cost = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)

    max_dist = torch.max(distance_matrix[knn_mask])
    max_dist = max_dist if max_dist > 0 else 1.0
    
    normalized_distances = distance_matrix / max_dist
    heuristic[knn_mask] = -0.8 * normalized_distances[knn_mask]
    
    # Distance-based clustering with adaptive epsilon
    # Determine epsilon as a fraction of average distance, adjusted by local density
    avg_dist = torch.mean(distance_matrix[distance_matrix > 0])  # exclude self-distances
    # Adjust epsilon based on local density - denser areas might need smaller epsilon
    local_density_normalized = normalized_local_density / normalized_local_density.mean()
    adaptive_epsilon_factor = torch.clamp(local_density_normalized, 0.2, 1.5)
    eps = avg_dist * 0.3 * adaptive_epsilon_factor.mean()  # use 30% of average distance as base clustering radius
    
    # Assign cluster labels using a simplified approach
    cluster_labels = torch.full((n,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=distance_matrix.device)
    current_cluster_id = 0
    
    # Efficient clustering using distance matrix directly
    visited = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i]:
            continue
        
        # Find neighbors within eps distance (excluding self)
        neighbors = torch.where((distance_matrix[i] <= eps) & (distance_matrix[i] > 0))[0]
        
        if len(neighbors) > 0:  # If we have neighbors
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            cluster_labels[neighbors] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            visited[neighbors] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
        else:
            # Isolated point goes to its own cluster
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1

    # Spatial clustering component - vectorized computation
    # Boost intra-cluster edges and penalize inter-cluster edges
    cluster_boost = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    
    # Vectorized cluster comparison
    cluster_i = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    cluster_j = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    # Identify intra-cluster edges
    intra_cluster_mask = (cluster_i == cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1)
    
    # Calculate cluster demands efficiently
    unique_clusters = torch.unique(cluster_labels)
    cluster_demands = torch.zeros(len(unique_clusters), device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        cluster_nodes = torch.where(cluster_labels == cluster_id)[0]
        cluster_demands[idx] = demands[cluster_nodes].sum()
    
    # Map cluster IDs to their demands
    cluster_demand_map = torch.zeros(current_cluster_id, device=distance_matrix.device)
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        if cluster_id >= 0:
            cluster_demand_map[cluster_id] = cluster_demands[idx]
    
    # Boost intra-cluster edges for reasonable demand clusters
    cluster_demand_i = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
    cluster_demand_j = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
    
    # Boost intra-cluster edges for reasonable demand clusters
    reasonable_demand_mask = (cluster_demand_i <= 2.0) & (cluster_demand_j <= 2.0)
    boost_mask = intra_cluster_mask & reasonable_demand_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[boost_mask] = 0.20  # Increased from 0.15 to give more incentive to intra-cluster edges
    
    # Penalize inter-cluster edges connecting high-demand clusters
    inter_cluster_mask = (cluster_i != cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1) & (cluster_j != -1)
    high_demand_inter_mask = (cluster_demand_i > avg_demand) & (cluster_demand_j > avg_demand)
    penalty_mask = inter_cluster_mask & high_demand_inter_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[penalty_mask] = -0.15  # Increased penalty from -0.1 to -0.15

    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + cluster_boost[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware component
    demand_i = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    demand_j = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    combined_demand_factor = (demand_i + demand_j) / (2 * avg_demand + 1e-8)
    capacity_adjustment = -0.05 * combined_demand_factor
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + capacity_adjustment[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware component: Consider individual demand ratios
    demand_ratio_i = demand_i / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    demand_ratio_j = demand_j / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    high_demand_connection_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_both = (demand_ratio_i > 1.0) & (demand_ratio_j > 1.0)
    high_demand_connection_penalty[high_demand_both] = -0.05
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_connection_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Depot connection adjustments
    depot_return_benefit = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    depot_exit_cost = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.18 * depot_return_benefit
    heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.12 * depot_exit_cost[1:]
    
    # For non-knn edges, assign large negative values to discourage their selection
    non_knn_mask = ~knn_mask & ~mask
    heuristic[non_knn_mask] = -10.0
    
    # Additional capacity constraint: penalize edges that connect high-demand nodes
    high_demand_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_threshold = avg_demand * 1.2
    
    high_demand_nodes = demands > high_demand_threshold
    high_demand_from = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(heuristic)
    high_demand_to = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(heuristic)
    
    high_demand_penalty[high_demand_from & high_demand_to] = -0.5
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Adjust based on dynamic k values - nodes with smaller neighborhoods get slightly higher incentives
    k_incentive = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    base_k_tensor = torch.tensor(base_k, dtype=torch.float, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].float()
        norm_k = k_i / base_k_tensor
        k_incentive[i, knn_mask[i]] = 0.05 * (1.0 - norm_k)
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + k_incentive[knn_mask]
    
    return heuristic

import torch
import math

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Efficient implementation of adaptive, demand-aware neighborhood graphs that 
    dynamically adjust connection thresholds per node based on local demand density and vehicle capacity constraints. 
    Constructs a hierarchical attention bias combining (1) distance-normalized edge weights, (2) intra-neighborhood 
    coherence bonuses, and (3) inter-neighborhood transition penalties scaled by residual vehicle capacity.

    Args:
        distance_matrix: A tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all pairs of nodes
        demands: A tensor of shape (n,) representing demands for each node (normalized by vehicle capacity)
        
    Returns:
        A tensor of same shape as distance_matrix with heuristic values.
        Negative values indicate undesirable edges, positive values indicate promising ones.
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    
    # Early return for small matrices
    if n <= 1:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Compute dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    sorted_dists, _ = torch.sort(distance_matrix, dim=1)
    
    k_max = min(n - 1, 20)
    k_min = 3
    k_for_avg = 5  # Use a fixed k to compute average distance for efficiency
    
    # Efficiently compute average distance for each node to its k nearest neighbors
    avg_dists_tensor = sorted_dists[:, 1:k_for_avg+1].mean(dim=1)  # Shape: (n,)
    
    # Compute local demand density efficiently using vectorized operations
    # Create a distance mask for neighbors within radius
    radius_tensor = avg_dists_tensor.unsqueeze(1)  # Shape: (n, 1)
    neighbor_mask = distance_matrix <= radius_tensor  # Shape: (n, n)
    
    # Expand demands for efficient computation
    expanded_demands = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)  # Shape: (n, n)
    masked_demands = expanded_demands * neighbor_mask.float()
    local_density = masked_demands.sum(dim=1)  # Sum over columns for each row
    
    total_demand = demands[1:].sum()
    avg_demand = total_demand / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 1.0
    normalized_local_density = local_density / avg_demand
    
    # Determine dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    base_k = max(5, int(n ** 0.5))
    density_factor = torch.clamp(2.0 / (1.0 + normalized_local_density), 0.5, 2.0)
    dynamic_k = torch.clamp((base_k * density_factor).int(), min=k_min, max=min(n-1, 15))
    
    # Create mask for k-nearest neighbors for each node (vectorized approach)
    mask = torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    knn_mask = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix, dtype=torch.bool)
    
    # Vectorized approach to create kNN mask
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].item()
        _, indices = torch.topk(distance_matrix[i], k=k_i+1, largest=False)
        # Remove self if present and take only k_i neighbors
        valid_indices = indices[indices != i][:k_i]
        knn_mask[i, valid_indices] = True
    
    # Initialize heuristic matrix
    heuristic = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # For k-nearest neighbors, assign values based on distance and capacity considerations
    max_dist = torch.max(distance_matrix[knn_mask])
    max_dist = max_dist if max_dist > 0 else 1.0
    
    normalized_distances = distance_matrix / max_dist
    heuristic[knn_mask] = -0.8 * normalized_distances[knn_mask]
    
    # Compute adaptive neighborhood graphs based on local demand density
    adaptive_thresholds = avg_dists_tensor * (1.0 + 0.5 * normalized_local_density)
    
    # Create demand-aware neighborhood masks efficiently
    threshold_expanded = adaptive_thresholds.unsqueeze(1)  # Shape: (n, 1)
    demand_neighborhood_mask = distance_matrix <= threshold_expanded  # Shape: (n, n)
    demand_neighborhood_mask.fill_diagonal_(False)  # Zero out diagonal
    
    # Calculate soft neighborhood memberships using Gaussian-weighted proximity
    sigma = avg_dists_tensor.mean()  # Use average distance as sigma for Gaussian kernel
    if sigma == 0:
        sigma = 1.0
    gaussian_weights = torch.exp(-distance_matrix ** 2 / (2 * sigma ** 2))
    gaussian_weights.fill_diagonal_(0)  # No self-connections
    
    # Normalize gaussian weights for each node to get soft membership probabilities
    row_sums = gaussian_weights.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    row_sums[row_sums == 0] = 1  # Avoid division by zero
    soft_membership = gaussian_weights / row_sums
    
    # Vectorized computation of intra-neighborhood coherence bonuses
    # Create masks for mutual neighborhoods
    mutual_nbhd_mask = demand_neighborhood_mask & demand_neighborhood_mask.transpose(0, 1)
    mutual_nbhd_mask = mutual_nbhd_mask & ~mask  # Exclude self connections
    
    # Compute demand compatibility efficiently
    demand_i = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    demand_j = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    demand_compatibility = 1.0 / (1.0 + torch.abs(demand_i - demand_j))
    intra_nbhd_bonus = 0.1 * soft_membership * demand_compatibility
    intra_nbhd_bonus = intra_nbhd_bonus * mutual_nbhd_mask.float()
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + intra_nbhd_bonus[knn_mask]
    
    # Inter-neighborhood transition penalties (vectorized approach)
    # Compute Jaccard similarity between neighborhoods efficiently
    intersection = (demand_neighborhood_mask.unsqueeze(1) & demand_neighborhood_mask.unsqueeze(0)).sum(dim=2).float()  # (n, n)
    union = (demand_neighborhood_mask.unsqueeze(1) | demand_neighborhood_mask.unsqueeze(0)).sum(dim=2).float()  # (n, n)
    
    jaccard_similarities = torch.where(union > 0, intersection / union, torch.zeros_like(intersection))
    low_jaccard_mask = (jaccard_similarities < 0.3) & ~mask  # Mask for different neighborhoods
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity and penalties
    combined_demand = demand_i + demand_j
    vehicle_capacity = 1.0
    remaining_capacity = vehicle_capacity - combined_demand
    penalty_factor = torch.clamp(1.0 - remaining_capacity / vehicle_capacity, min=0.0)
    inter_nbhd_penalty = -0.1 * penalty_factor * normalized_distances
    inter_nbhd_penalty = inter_nbhd_penalty * low_jaccard_mask.float()
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + inter_nbhd_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware components
    combined_demand_factor = (demand_i + demand_j) / (2 * avg_demand + 1e-8)
    capacity_adjustment = -0.05 * combined_demand_factor
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + capacity_adjustment[knn_mask]
    
    # High demand connection penalties
    demand_ratio_i = demand_i / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    demand_ratio_j = demand_j / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    high_demand_both = (demand_ratio_i > 1.0) & (demand_ratio_j > 1.0)
    high_demand_connection_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_connection_penalty[high_demand_both] = -0.05
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_connection_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Depot connection adjustments
    depot_return_benefit = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    depot_exit_cost = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.18 * depot_return_benefit
    heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.12 * depot_exit_cost[1:]
    
    # For non-knn edges, assign large negative values to discourage their selection
    non_knn_mask = ~knn_mask & ~mask
    heuristic[non_knn_mask] = -10.0
    
    # Additional capacity constraint: penalize edges that connect high-demand nodes
    high_demand_threshold = avg_demand * 1.2
    high_demand_nodes = demands > high_demand_threshold
    high_demand_from = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(heuristic)
    high_demand_to = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(heuristic)
    
    high_demand_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_penalty[high_demand_from & high_demand_to] = -0.5
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Adjust based on dynamic k values - nodes with smaller neighborhoods get slightly higher incentives
    base_k_tensor = torch.tensor(base_k, dtype=torch.float, device=distance_matrix.device)
    norm_k = dynamic_k.float() / base_k_tensor
    k_incentive_per_node = 0.05 * (1.0 - norm_k)  # Shape: (n,)
    k_incentive = k_incentive_per_node.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)  # Shape: (n, n)
    k_incentive = k_incentive * knn_mask.float()
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + k_incentive[knn_mask]
    
    return heuristic

import torch
import math

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Clean implementation based on the successful parent solution with improvements.
    Uses distance-based clustering and dynamic k-NN approach with enhanced clustering parameters.
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: A tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all pairs of nodes
        demands: A tensor of shape (n,) representing demands for each node (normalized by vehicle capacity)
        
    Returns:
        A tensor of same shape as distance_matrix with heuristic values.
        Negative values indicate undesirable edges, positive values indicate promising ones.
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    
    # Early return for small matrices
    if n <= 1:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Compute dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    sorted_dists, _ = torch.sort(distance_matrix, dim=1)
    
    k_max = min(n - 1, 20)
    k_min = 3
    
    avg_dists = []
    for i in range(k_min, k_max + 1):
        avg_dist = sorted_dists[:, 1:i+1].mean(dim=1)
        avg_dists.append(avg_dist.unsqueeze(0))
    
    avg_dists_tensor = torch.cat(avg_dists, dim=0).mean(dim=0)
    
    # Compute local demand density efficiently
    # Calculate average distance for each node to determine neighborhood size
    local_density = torch.zeros(n, device=distance_matrix.device)
    for i in range(n):
        radius = avg_dists_tensor[i]
        neighbors_mask = distance_matrix[i, :] <= radius
        local_density[i] = demands[neighbors_mask].sum()
    
    total_demand = demands[1:].sum()
    avg_demand = total_demand / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 1.0
    normalized_local_density = local_density / avg_demand
    
    # Determine dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    base_k = max(5, int(n ** 0.5))
    density_factor = torch.clamp(2.0 / (1.0 + normalized_local_density), 0.5, 2.0)
    dynamic_k = torch.clamp((base_k * density_factor).int(), min=k_min, max=min(n-1, 15))
    
    # Create mask for k-nearest neighbors for each node (dynamic k) - vectorized
    mask = torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    knn_mask = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix, dtype=torch.bool)
    
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].item()
        _, indices = torch.topk(distance_matrix[i], k=k_i+1, largest=False)
        # Remove self if present and take only k_i neighbors
        valid_indices = indices[indices != i][:k_i]
        knn_mask[i, valid_indices] = True
    
    # Initialize heuristic matrix
    heuristic = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # For k-nearest neighbors, assign values based on distance and capacity considerations
    max_dist = torch.max(distance_matrix[knn_mask])
    max_dist = max_dist if max_dist > 0 else 1.0
    
    normalized_distances = distance_matrix / max_dist
    heuristic[knn_mask] = -0.8 * normalized_distances[knn_mask]
    
    # Distance-based clustering with adaptive epsilon
    # Determine epsilon as a fraction of average distance, adjusted by local density
    avg_dist = torch.mean(distance_matrix[distance_matrix > 0])  # exclude self-distances
    # Adjust epsilon based on local density - denser areas might need smaller epsilon
    local_density_normalized = normalized_local_density / normalized_local_density.mean()
    adaptive_epsilon_factor = torch.clamp(local_density_normalized, 0.2, 1.5)
    eps = avg_dist * 0.3 * adaptive_epsilon_factor.mean()  # use 30% of average distance as base clustering radius
    
    # Assign cluster labels using a simplified approach
    cluster_labels = torch.full((n,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=distance_matrix.device)
    current_cluster_id = 0
    
    # Efficient clustering using distance matrix directly
    visited = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i]:
            continue
        
        # Find neighbors within eps distance (excluding self)
        neighbors = torch.where((distance_matrix[i] <= eps) & (distance_matrix[i] > 0))[0]
        
        if len(neighbors) > 0:  # If we have neighbors
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            cluster_labels[neighbors] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            visited[neighbors] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
        else:
            # Isolated point goes to its own cluster
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1

    # Spatial clustering component - vectorized computation
    # Boost intra-cluster edges and penalize inter-cluster edges
    cluster_boost = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    
    # Vectorized cluster comparison
    cluster_i = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    cluster_j = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    # Identify intra-cluster edges
    intra_cluster_mask = (cluster_i == cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1)
    
    # Calculate cluster demands efficiently
    unique_clusters = torch.unique(cluster_labels)
    cluster_demands = torch.zeros(len(unique_clusters), device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        cluster_nodes = torch.where(cluster_labels == cluster_id)[0]
        cluster_demands[idx] = demands[cluster_nodes].sum()
    
    # Map cluster IDs to their demands
    cluster_demand_map = torch.zeros(current_cluster_id, device=distance_matrix.device)
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        if cluster_id >= 0:
            cluster_demand_map[cluster_id] = cluster_demands[idx]
    
    # Boost intra-cluster edges for reasonable demand clusters
    cluster_demand_i = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
    cluster_demand_j = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
    
    # Boost intra-cluster edges for reasonable demand clusters
    reasonable_demand_mask = (cluster_demand_i <= 2.0) & (cluster_demand_j <= 2.0)
    boost_mask = intra_cluster_mask & reasonable_demand_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[boost_mask] = 0.20  # Increased from 0.15 to give more incentive to intra-cluster edges
    
    # Penalize inter-cluster edges connecting high-demand clusters
    inter_cluster_mask = (cluster_i != cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1) & (cluster_j != -1)
    high_demand_inter_mask = (cluster_demand_i > avg_demand) & (cluster_demand_j > avg_demand)
    penalty_mask = inter_cluster_mask & high_demand_inter_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[penalty_mask] = -0.15  # Increased penalty from -0.1 to -0.15

    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + cluster_boost[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware component
    demand_i = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    demand_j = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    combined_demand_factor = (demand_i + demand_j) / (2 * avg_demand + 1e-8)
    capacity_adjustment = -0.05 * combined_demand_factor
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + capacity_adjustment[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware component: Consider individual demand ratios
    demand_ratio_i = demand_i / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    demand_ratio_j = demand_j / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    high_demand_connection_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_both = (demand_ratio_i > 1.0) & (demand_ratio_j > 1.0)
    high_demand_connection_penalty[high_demand_both] = -0.05
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_connection_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Depot connection adjustments
    depot_return_benefit = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    depot_exit_cost = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.18 * depot_return_benefit
    heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.12 * depot_exit_cost[1:]
    
    # For non-knn edges, assign large negative values to discourage their selection
    non_knn_mask = ~knn_mask & ~mask
    heuristic[non_knn_mask] = -10.0
    
    # Additional capacity constraint: penalize edges that connect high-demand nodes
    high_demand_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_threshold = avg_demand * 1.2
    
    high_demand_nodes = demands > high_demand_threshold
    high_demand_from = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(heuristic)
    high_demand_to = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(heuristic)
    
    high_demand_penalty[high_demand_from & high_demand_to] = -0.5
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Adjust based on dynamic k values - nodes with smaller neighborhoods get slightly higher incentives
    k_incentive = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    base_k_tensor = torch.tensor(base_k, dtype=torch.float, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].float()
        norm_k = k_i / base_k_tensor
        k_incentive[i, knn_mask[i]] = 0.05 * (1.0 - norm_k)
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + k_incentive[knn_mask]
    
    return heuristic

    # Heat kernel diffusion for continuous spatial coherence
    # Compute Gaussian similarity matrix based on adaptive radii
    # Each node has its own characteristic scale
    gaussian_similarities = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    for i in range(n):
        # Use adaptive radius for each node as the scale parameter
        sigma = adaptive_radius[i] / 3.0  # Use 1/3 of radius as std for Gaussian
        # Prevent division by zero
        sigma = torch.clamp(sigma, min=1e-6)
        gaussian_similarities[i, :] = torch.exp(-0.5 * (distance_matrix[i, :] / sigma) ** 2)
    
    # Normalize the similarities row-wise to get transition probabilities
    row_sum = gaussian_similarities.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    row_sum = torch.clamp(row_sum, min=1e-6)  # Avoid division by zero
    transition_probs = gaussian_similarities / row_sum
    
    # Apply heat kernel diffusion to propagate spatial coherence
    # Use a small time parameter for short-time diffusion
    t = 0.1
    # Compute the diffusion matrix (approximated)
    # I + t*L where L is the normalized Laplacian, but for simplicity use transition matrix
    diffusion_weights = (1 - t) * torch.eye(n, device=distance_matrix.device) + t * transition_probs
    
    # Compute spatial coherence scores using diffusion
    spatial_coherence = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    for i in range(n):
        # Propagate local information using diffusion
        propagated_values = diffusion_weights[i, :].unsqueeze(1) * gaussian_similarities
        # Take the average propagated similarity as coherence measure
        coherence_scores = propagated_values.mean(dim=0)
        spatial_coherence[i, :] = coherence_scores
    
    # Boost edges with high spatial coherence within k-NN
    coherence_boost = 0.2 * spatial_coherence
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + coherence_boost[knn_mask]

    # Simplified clustering using distance matrix directly (from parent solution)
    # Determine epsilon as a fraction of average distance
    avg_dist = torch.mean(distance_matrix[distance_matrix > 0])  # exclude self-distances
    eps = avg_dist * 0.3  # use 30% of average distance as clustering radius
    
    # Assign cluster labels using a simplified approach
    cluster_labels = torch.full((n,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=distance_matrix.device)
    current_cluster_id = 0
    
    # Efficient clustering using distance matrix directly
    visited = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i]:
            continue
        
        # Find neighbors within eps distance (excluding self)
        neighbors = torch.where((distance_matrix[i] <= eps) & (distance_matrix[i] > 0))[0]
        
        if len(neighbors) > 0:  # If we have neighbors
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            cluster_labels[neighbors] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            visited[neighbors] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
        else:
            # Isolated point goes to its own cluster
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1

    # Spatial clustering component - vectorized computation
    # Boost intra-cluster edges and penalize inter-cluster edges
    cluster_boost = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    
    # Vectorized cluster comparison
    cluster_i = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    cluster_j = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    # Identify intra-cluster edges
    intra_cluster_mask = (cluster_i == cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1)
    
    # Calculate cluster demands efficiently
    unique_clusters = torch.unique(cluster_labels)
    cluster_demands = torch.zeros(len(unique_clusters), device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        cluster_nodes = torch.where(cluster_labels == cluster_id)[0]
        cluster_demands[idx] = demands[cluster_nodes].sum()
    
    # Map cluster IDs to their demands
    cluster_demand_map = torch.zeros(current_cluster_id, device=distance_matrix.device)
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        if cluster_id >= 0:
            cluster_demand_map[cluster_id] = cluster_demands[idx]
    
    # Boost intra-cluster edges for reasonable demand clusters
    cluster_demand_i = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
    cluster_demand_j = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
    
    # Boost intra-cluster edges for reasonable demand clusters
    reasonable_demand_mask = (cluster_demand_i <= 2.0) & (cluster_demand_j <= 2.0)
    boost_mask = intra_cluster_mask & reasonable_demand_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[boost_mask] = 0.15
    
    # Penalize inter-cluster edges connecting high-demand clusters
    inter_cluster_mask = (cluster_i != cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1) & (cluster_j != -1)
    high_demand_inter_mask = (cluster_demand_i > avg_demand) & (cluster_demand_j > avg_demand)
    penalty_mask = inter_cluster_mask & high_demand_inter_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[penalty_mask] = -0.1
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + cluster_boost[knn_mask]

import torch

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Implementation idea: Develop a hybrid heuristic that integrates dynamic residual capacity estimation 
    with learned edge preferences by simulating partial routes from each node to estimate feasible 
    future loads, then using these estimates to modulate the attention bias. Specifically, for each 
    node i, compute a 'remaining capacity profile' based on its demand and the average demand of its 
    k-nearest neighbors, then adjust the edge score for (i,j) by a factor that reflects whether adding 
    j would likely exceed capacity given this local context. This addresses the key limitation 
    identified in Parent #1—that local capacity feasibility is hard to estimate without route 
    construction—while preserving the strong distance-based foundation and avoiding the complexity 
    of full online learning used in Parent #2.
    
    Implementation considerations:
    - Use k-nearest neighbors to define local contexts around each node
    - Estimate remaining capacity based on local demand density
    - Apply capacity-based penalties that vary based on local demand profiles
    - Preserve strong distance-based foundation from parent solutions
    - Use depot-specific heuristics that adapt to problem size
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: A tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all pairs of nodes
        demands: A tensor of shape (n,) representing demands for each node (normalized by vehicle capacity)
        
    Returns:
        A tensor of same shape as distance_matrix with heuristic values.
        Negative values indicate undesirable edges, positive values indicate promising ones.
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    
    # Early return for small matrices
    if n <= 1:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Create a mask for k-nearest neighbors (excluding self-loops)
    k = max(5, int(n ** 0.5))  # At least 5 nearest neighbors, scaled with problem size
    
    # Create mask to exclude diagonal (self loops)
    mask = torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    # Find k nearest neighbors for each node (excluding self)
    _, indices = torch.topk(distance_matrix, k=k+1, largest=False, dim=1)  # +1 to account for self
    
    # Create a sparse mask for k-nearest neighbors
    knn_mask = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix, dtype=torch.bool)
    row_indices = torch.arange(n, device=distance_matrix.device).unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, k+1)
    knn_mask[row_indices, indices] = True
    # Remove self loops from the knn mask
    knn_mask[mask] = False
    
    # Initialize heuristic matrix
    heuristic = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Distance-based component (primary signal)
    max_dist = torch.max(distance_matrix[knn_mask]) if torch.any(knn_mask) else 1.0
    max_dist = max_dist if max_dist > 0 else 1.0
    
    normalized_distances = distance_matrix / max_dist
    # Make distance-based heuristic more impactful: -0.8 instead of just negative normalized distance
    heuristic[knn_mask] = -0.8 * normalized_distances[knn_mask]
    
    # Calculate problem statistics
    total_demand = demands[1:].sum()  # Exclude depot
    avg_demand = total_demand / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 1.0
    
    # Calculate local demand density for each node
    local_avg_demand = torch.zeros(n, device=demands.device)
    for i in range(n):
        k_neighbors = indices[i, 1:k+1]  # Exclude self (first element)
        local_avg_demand[i] = demands[k_neighbors].mean() if len(k_neighbors) > 0 else avg_demand
    
    # Capacity-aware component: estimate remaining capacity based on local context
    demand_i = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)  # Demand of source node i
    demand_j = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)  # Demand of destination node j
    
    # Calculate capacity factor: consider local demand density when evaluating edge feasibility
    local_density_i = local_avg_demand.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    local_density_j = local_avg_demand.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    # Combined local density factor for edge (i, j)
    combined_local_density = (local_density_i + local_density_j) / (2 * avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    # Capacity adjustment based on local density context
    # When local density is high, be more cautious about connecting nodes
    capacity_adjustment = -0.15 * combined_local_density  # Negative because higher density is less favorable
    
    # Apply capacity adjustment to k-nearest neighbors
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + capacity_adjustment[knn_mask]
    
    # Depot-specific logic
    depot_return_benefit = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    depot_exit_cost = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    
    # Benefit for returning to depot after visiting high-demand nodes
    depot_return_benefit[:, 0] = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    # Cost for leaving depot to visit high-demand initial customers
    depot_exit_cost[0, :] = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    # Apply depot benefits/costs with size-dependent scaling
    if n >= 500:
        # Stronger depot incentives for larger problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.18 * depot_return_benefit[:, 0]
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.10 * depot_exit_cost[0, 1:]
    elif n <= 200:
        # More conservative depot incentives for smaller problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.12 * depot_return_benefit[:, 0]
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.07 * depot_exit_cost[0, 1:]
    else:
        # Default depot incentives for medium-sized problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.15 * depot_return_benefit[:, 0]
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.08 * depot_exit_cost[0, 1:]
    
    # High-demand penalty: discourage connecting very high-demand nodes together
    high_demand_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_threshold = avg_demand * 1.5  # Threshold for what constitutes "very high" demand
    
    # Identify very high-demand nodes
    very_high_demand_nodes = demands > high_demand_threshold
    very_high_demand_from = very_high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(heuristic)
    very_high_demand_to = very_high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(heuristic)
    
    # Apply severe penalty when going from very high-demand to very high-demand node
    high_demand_penalty[very_high_demand_from & very_high_demand_to] = -0.6
    
    # Also apply moderate penalty for high-demand nodes (not as severe)
    high_demand_threshold_mild = avg_demand * 1.2
    high_demand_nodes = demands > high_demand_threshold_mild
    high_demand_from = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(heuristic)
    high_demand_to = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(heuristic)
    
    # Only apply high demand penalty where not already applied severely
    mild_penalty_mask = (high_demand_from & high_demand_to) & ~(very_high_demand_from & very_high_demand_to)
    high_demand_penalty[mild_penalty_mask] = -0.3
    
    # Apply high demand penalty to k-nn edges
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # For non-knn edges, assign large negative values to discourage their selection
    non_knn_mask = ~knn_mask & ~mask  # Exclude self loops
    heuristic[non_knn_mask] = -10.0
    
    # Additional residual capacity estimation: For each node, estimate how many additional nodes
    # could be served given its demand and local context
    remaining_capacity_factor = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    for i in range(n):
        # Estimate available capacity if we start from node i
        est_remaining_capacity = 1.0 - demands[i]  # Assuming unit capacity vehicle
        k_neighbors = indices[i, 1:k+1]  # Exclude self
        
        if len(k_neighbors) > 0:
            # Estimate how much demand we might encounter in next steps
            est_future_demand = demands[k_neighbors].sum() / len(k_neighbors)  # Average demand of neighbors
            if est_future_demand > 0:
                est_nodes_fittable = est_remaining_capacity / est_future_demand
                # Higher score if more nodes can potentially fit
                remaining_capacity_factor[i, k_neighbors] = torch.clamp(est_nodes_fittable, 0.0, 1.0)
    
    # Apply remaining capacity factor to heuristic (only for knn edges)
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + 0.1 * remaining_capacity_factor[knn_mask]
    
    return heuristic

import torch

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Implementation idea: Simplified heuristic based on Parent #2's successful approach but refined.
    Focus on distance-based foundation with basic demand compatibility and depot handling.
    This addresses the over-complication issue in the current solution while preserving
    effective elements from successful parent solutions.
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: A tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all pairs of nodes
        demands: A tensor of shape (n,) representing demands for each node (normalized by vehicle capacity)
        
    Returns:
        A tensor of same shape as distance_matrix with heuristic values.
        Negative values indicate undesirable edges, positive values indicate promising ones.
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    
    # Early return for small matrices
    if n <= 1:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Create a mask for k-nearest neighbors (excluding self-loops)
    k = max(5, int(n ** 0.5))  # At least 5 nearest neighbors, scaled with problem size
    
    # Create mask to exclude diagonal (self loops)
    mask = torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    # Find k nearest neighbors for each node (excluding self)
    _, indices = torch.topk(distance_matrix, k=k+1, largest=False, dim=1)  # +1 to account for self
    
    # Create a sparse mask for k-nearest neighbors
    knn_mask = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix, dtype=torch.bool)
    row_indices = torch.arange(n, device=distance_matrix.device).unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, k+1)
    knn_mask[row_indices, indices] = True
    # Remove self loops from the knn mask
    knn_mask[mask] = False
    
    # Initialize heuristic matrix
    heuristic = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Distance-based component (primary signal)
    max_dist = torch.max(distance_matrix[knn_mask]) if torch.any(knn_mask) else 1.0
    max_dist = max_dist if max_dist > 0 else 1.0
    
    normalized_distances = distance_matrix / max_dist
    # Make distance-based heuristic more impactful: -0.8 instead of just negative normalized distance
    heuristic[knn_mask] = -0.8 * normalized_distances[knn_mask]
    
    # Calculate problem statistics
    total_demand = demands[1:].sum()  # Exclude depot
    avg_demand = total_demand / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 1.0
    
    # Demand compatibility component: penalize edges between nodes with high combined demand
    demand_i = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)  # Demand of source node i
    demand_j = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)  # Demand of destination node j
    
    # Combined demand factor - higher combined demand is generally less favorable
    combined_demand_factor = (demand_i + demand_j) / (2 * avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    # Apply demand compatibility adjustment to k-nearest neighbors
    demand_adjustment = -0.12 * combined_demand_factor
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + demand_adjustment[knn_mask]
    
    # Depot-specific logic with simplified approach
    depot_return_benefit = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    depot_exit_cost = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    
    # Benefit for returning to depot after visiting high-demand nodes
    depot_return_benefit[:, 0] = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    # Cost for leaving depot to visit high-demand initial customers
    depot_exit_cost[0, :] = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    # Apply depot benefits/costs with size-dependent scaling
    if n >= 500:
        # Stronger depot incentives for larger problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.18 * depot_return_benefit[:, 0]
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.10 * depot_exit_cost[0, 1:]
    elif n <= 200:
        # More conservative depot incentives for smaller problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.12 * depot_return_benefit[:, 0]
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.07 * depot_exit_cost[0, 1:]
    else:
        # Default depot incentives for medium-sized problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.15 * depot_return_benefit[:, 0]
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.08 * depot_exit_cost[0, 1:]
    
    # High-demand penalty: discourage connecting high-demand nodes together
    high_demand_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_threshold = avg_demand * 1.3  # Threshold for high demand nodes
    
    # Identify high-demand nodes
    high_demand_nodes = demands > high_demand_threshold
    high_demand_from = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(heuristic)
    high_demand_to = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(heuristic)
    
    # Apply penalty when going from high-demand to high-demand node
    high_demand_penalty[high_demand_from & high_demand_to] = -0.4
    
    # Apply high demand penalty to k-nn edges
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # For non-knn edges, assign large negative values to discourage their selection
    non_knn_mask = ~knn_mask & ~mask  # Exclude self loops
    heuristic[non_knn_mask] = -10.0
    
    return heuristic

import torch

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Implementation idea: Adopt Parent #2's successful MLP-based approach with integrated features.
    Use a weighted combination of normalized distance, demand_i, demand_j, and cluster similarity
    to create a more cohesive heuristic signal. This follows the approach that achieved the 
    best performance (67.728) while potentially refining parameters.
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: A tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all pairs of nodes
        demands: A tensor of shape (n,) representing demands for each node (normalized by vehicle capacity)
        
    Returns:
        A tensor of same shape as distance_matrix with heuristic values.
        Negative values indicate undesirable edges, positive values indicate promising ones.
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    
    # Early return for small matrices
    if n <= 1:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Extract coordinates using classical multidimensional scaling (MDS) approximation
    H = torch.eye(n, device=distance_matrix.device) - (1.0 / n) * torch.ones(n, n, device=distance_matrix.device)
    D_squared = distance_matrix ** 2
    B = -0.5 * H @ D_squared @ H
    eigenvals, eigenvecs = torch.linalg.eigh(B)
    idx = torch.argsort(eigenvals, descending=True)[:2]
    coords = eigenvecs[:, idx] * torch.sqrt(torch.abs(eigenvals[idx]))
    
    # Simple clustering using distance-based approach
    avg_dist = torch.mean(distance_matrix[distance_matrix > 0])
    eps = avg_dist * 0.3
    
    cluster_labels = torch.full((n,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=distance_matrix.device)
    current_cluster_id = 0
    visited = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i]:
            continue
        
        neighbors = torch.where((distance_matrix[i] <= eps) & (distance_matrix[i] > 0))[0]
        
        if len(neighbors) > 0:
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            cluster_labels[neighbors] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            visited[neighbors] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
        else:
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
    
    # Compute dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    sorted_dists, _ = torch.sort(distance_matrix, dim=1)
    
    k_max = min(n - 1, 20)
    k_min = 3
    
    avg_dists = []
    for i in range(k_min, k_max + 1):
        avg_dist = sorted_dists[:, 1:i+1].mean(dim=1)
        avg_dists.append(avg_dist.unsqueeze(0))
    
    avg_dists_tensor = torch.cat(avg_dists, dim=0).mean(dim=0)
    
    # Compute local demand density
    local_density = torch.zeros(n, device=distance_matrix.device)
    for i in range(n):
        radius = avg_dists_tensor[i]
        neighbors_mask = distance_matrix[i, :] <= radius
        local_density[i] = demands[neighbors_mask].sum()
    
    avg_demand = demands[1:].sum() / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 1.0
    normalized_local_density = local_density / avg_demand
    
    # Determine dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    base_k = max(5, int(n ** 0.5))
    density_factor = torch.clamp(2.0 / (1.0 + normalized_local_density), 0.5, 2.0)
    dynamic_k = torch.clamp((base_k * density_factor).int(), min=k_min, max=min(n-1, 15))
    
    # Create mask for k-nearest neighbors for each node (dynamic k)
    mask = torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    knn_mask = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix, dtype=torch.bool)
    
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].item()
        _, indices = torch.topk(distance_matrix[i], k=k_i+1, largest=False)
        valid_indices = indices[indices != i][:k_i]
        knn_mask[i, valid_indices] = True
    
    # Prepare features for the integrated MLP-like computation
    # Features: normalized distance, demand_i, demand_j, cluster similarity
    max_dist = torch.max(distance_matrix[knn_mask]) if torch.any(knn_mask) else 1.0
    max_dist = max_dist if max_dist > 0 else 1.0
    
    # Normalize distance matrix
    normalized_distances = distance_matrix / max_dist
    
    # Demand features
    demand_i_expanded = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    demand_j_expanded = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    # Cluster features
    cluster_i = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    cluster_j = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    same_cluster = (cluster_i == cluster_j).float()
    
    # Prepare input to the MLP-like computation
    # Shape: (n, n, 4) - distance, demand_i, demand_j, same_cluster
    features = torch.stack([
        normalized_distances,
        demand_i_expanded / (avg_demand + 1e-8),
        demand_j_expanded / (avg_demand + 1e-8),
        same_cluster
    ], dim=-1)  # Shape: (n, n, 4)
    
    # Define weights similar to Parent #2's MLP simulation
    weights = torch.tensor([-0.8, -0.1, -0.1, 0.2], device=features.device, dtype=features.dtype)
    # Bias term
    bias = torch.tensor([0.05], device=features.device, dtype=features.dtype)
    
    # Apply linear transformation
    linear_output = torch.sum(features * weights, dim=-1) + bias
    
    # Apply activation (tanh for bounded output)
    mlp_bias = torch.tanh(linear_output)
    
    # Initialize heuristic matrix
    heuristic = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Apply the MLP-based bias to k-nearest neighbors
    heuristic[knn_mask] = mlp_bias[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced depot-specific logic with size-dependent scaling
    depot_return_benefit = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    depot_exit_cost = demands / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    # Scale depot incentives based on problem size
    if n >= 500:
        # Stronger depot incentives for larger problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.20 * depot_return_benefit
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.12 * depot_exit_cost[1:]
    elif n <= 200:
        # More conservative depot incentives for smaller problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.12 * depot_return_benefit
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.08 * depot_exit_cost[1:]
    else:
        # Default depot incentives for medium-sized problems
        heuristic[:, 0] = heuristic[:, 0] + 0.15 * depot_return_benefit
        heuristic[0, 1:] = heuristic[0, 1:] - 0.1 * depot_exit_cost[1:]
    
    # For non-knn edges, assign large negative values to discourage their selection
    non_knn_mask = ~knn_mask & ~mask
    heuristic[non_knn_mask] = -10.0
    
    return heuristic

The latest round of experiments reinforces and refines the core principles established in prior research, while exposing critical boundaries of what static heuristics can achieve in the POMO framework for CVRP. First, **simplicity with precise calibration consistently outperforms complexity**: across all ten experiments, no adaptive, learned, or diffusion-based spatial coherence method has surpassed the performance of fixed epsilon clustering (ε = 0.3 × avg_dist) combined with dynamic k-NN based on local demand density. This confirms that POMO’s attention mechanism thrives on crisp, interpretable geometric signals rather than continuous or probabilistic fields, especially at scale (n=1000). Second, **the integration architecture matters more than component novelty**: Experiment #10’s success with an MLP-style weighted combination of distance, demands, and cluster similarity (score: 67.570) demonstrates that even hand-crafted feature fusion—when properly balanced (e.g., -0.8 distance weight, +0.2 cluster boost)—can yield gains, but only when built atop a stable backbone. In contrast, attempts to replace this backbone with GNNs, heat kernels, or multi-scale diffusion (Experiments #3, #7, #9) uniformly degraded performance, revealing that representational sophistication without alignment to POMO’s decoding dynamics is counterproductive. Third, **capacity awareness must be local and aggressive, not global or predictive**: efforts to estimate residual capacity or simulate partial routes (Experiments #6, #10 early variants) introduced noise rather than signal, whereas simple, strong penalties on high-demand edges (demand_i + demand_j > 0.8) remain effective. This underscores that static heuristics cannot—and should not attempt to—mimic sequential state; instead, they should flag *obvious* infeasibilities. Fourth, **depot handling benefits from asymmetry but resists over-engineering**: asymmetric incentives based on demand/distance efficiency (Experiment #3) provide measurable gains, but further refinements (e.g., size-adaptive scaling in Experiment #4) failed to improve large-instance performance, suggesting a ceiling for depot-specific tuning. Critically, **a scalability gap persists**: no heuristic configuration excels uniformly across n=200, 500, and 1000, with 1000-node instances consistently exposing fragility in complex methods. The repeated failure of vectorized, loop-free implementations (Experiment #2) also highlights a tension between computational efficiency and heuristic fidelity—sometimes, controlled per-node logic is necessary for quality. These insights shift future priorities toward three focused directions: (1) **robust, coordinate-free clustering** using only distance matrix neighborhoods with demand-weighted linkage, avoiding MDS or coordinate reconstruction entirely; (2) **learned yet constrained fusion weights**—training a tiny MLP offline on synthetic data to predict optimal combination coefficients for distance, demand, and cluster signals, but freezing them during inference to maintain stability; and (3) **directional inter-customer biases** that extend depot asymmetry to customer edges, penalizing transitions from low- to high-demand nodes when such moves are likely to strain residual capacity. The overarching lesson is clear: progress lies not in adding new signals, but in refining the contextual scaling, directional logic, and integration discipline of a minimal set of proven components—distance, demand, discrete clusters, and depot flow—while accepting the inherent limitations of static guidance in a dynamic routing process.

import torch

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Implementation idea: Replace coordinate-based MDS clustering with a coordinate-free, demand-weighted neighborhood 
    clustering approach that uses only the distance matrix and demands to define clusters via iterative expansion of 
    high-density regions. This avoids eigen-decomposition entirely to improve robustness and scalability while 
    maintaining the successful elements from parent solutions: dynamic k-NN based on local demand density, 
    capacity-aware penalties, and asymmetric depot handling. The clustering is performed directly on the distance 
    matrix by identifying dense regions where nodes are close together and have significant combined demand.
    
    Implementation considerations:
    - Use distance matrix neighborhoods to form clusters without coordinate reconstruction
    - Apply iterative expansion based on distance and demand thresholds
    - Maintain dynamic k-NN selection based on local demand density
    - Preserve capacity-aware penalties and asymmetric depot handling
    - Ensure computational efficiency by avoiding expensive matrix operations
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: A tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all pairs of nodes
        demands: A tensor of shape (n,) representing demands for each node (normalized by vehicle capacity)
        
    Returns:
        A tensor of same shape as distance_matrix with heuristic values.
        Negative values indicate undesirable edges, positive values indicate promising ones.
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    
    # Early return for small matrices
    if n <= 1:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Coordinate-free clustering using distance matrix neighborhoods
    cluster_labels = torch.full((n,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=distance_matrix.device)
    current_cluster_id = 0
    
    # Determine epsilon as a fraction of average distance
    avg_dist = torch.mean(distance_matrix[distance_matrix > 0])  # exclude self-distances
    eps = avg_dist * 0.3  # use 30% of average distance as clustering radius
    
    # Sort distances for each node to efficiently find neighbors
    sorted_dists, sorted_indices = torch.sort(distance_matrix, dim=1)
    
    # Perform clustering using distance neighborhoods
    visited = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i]:
            continue
            
        # Find neighbors within epsilon distance (excluding self)
        # Use sorted distances to efficiently find neighbors
        neighbor_mask = (sorted_dists[i, 1:] <= eps)  # Exclude self-distance at index 0
        neighbor_indices = sorted_indices[i, 1:][neighbor_mask]
        
        # Check if there are enough neighbors with sufficient demand to form a cluster
        if len(neighbor_indices) > 0:
            # Include the center node
            cluster_nodes = torch.cat([torch.tensor([i], device=distance_matrix.device), neighbor_indices])
            cluster_labels[cluster_nodes] = current_cluster_id
            visited[cluster_nodes] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
        else:
            # Isolated point gets its own cluster
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
    
    # Compute dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    k_max = min(n - 1, 20)
    k_min = 3
    
    # Compute local density for each node
    local_density = torch.zeros(n, device=distance_matrix.device)
    for i in range(n):
        # Find k neighbors based on distance
        k = min(k_max, n - 1)
        _, indices = torch.topk(distance_matrix[i], k=k+1, largest=False)
        # Remove self if present
        valid_indices = indices[indices != i][:k]
        
        # Calculate local density as sum of demands within average distance
        if len(valid_indices) > 0:
            local_density[i] = demands[valid_indices].sum()
    
    total_demand = demands[1:].sum()  # Exclude depot
    avg_demand = total_demand / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 1.0
    normalized_local_density = local_density / avg_demand
    
    # Determine dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    base_k = max(5, int(n ** 0.5))
    density_factor = torch.clamp(2.0 / (1.0 + normalized_local_density), 0.5, 2.0)
    dynamic_k = torch.clamp((base_k * density_factor).int(), min=k_min, max=min(n-1, 15))
    
    # Create mask for k-nearest neighbors for each node (dynamic k)
    mask = torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    knn_mask = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix, dtype=torch.bool)
    
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].item()
        _, indices = torch.topk(distance_matrix[i], k=k_i+1, largest=False)
        # Remove self if present and take only k_i neighbors
        valid_indices = indices[indices != i][:k_i]
        knn_mask[i, valid_indices] = True
    
    # Initialize heuristic matrix
    heuristic = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # For k-nearest neighbors, assign values based on distance and capacity considerations
    max_dist = torch.max(distance_matrix[knn_mask])
    max_dist = max_dist if max_dist > 0 else 1.0
    
    normalized_distances = distance_matrix / max_dist
    heuristic[knn_mask] = -0.75 * normalized_distances[knn_mask]  # Slightly reduced from -0.8 to allow more flexibility
    
    # Capacity-aware component
    demand_i = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    demand_j = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    combined_demand_factor = (demand_i + demand_j) / (2 * avg_demand + 1e-8)
    capacity_adjustment = -0.05 * combined_demand_factor
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + capacity_adjustment[knn_mask]
    
    # Individual demand ratio penalties
    demand_ratio_i = demand_i / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    demand_ratio_j = demand_j / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    high_demand_connection_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_both = (demand_ratio_i > 1.0) & (demand_ratio_j > 1.0)
    high_demand_connection_penalty[high_demand_both] = -0.05
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_connection_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Spatial clustering component - boost intra-cluster edges
    cluster_boost = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    
    # Vectorized cluster comparison
    cluster_i = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    cluster_j = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    # Identify intra-cluster edges
    intra_cluster_mask = (cluster_i == cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1) & (cluster_i >= 0)
    
    # Calculate cluster demands efficiently
    unique_clusters = torch.unique(cluster_labels[cluster_labels >= 0])
    cluster_demands = torch.zeros(len(unique_clusters), device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        cluster_nodes = torch.where(cluster_labels == cluster_id)[0]
        cluster_demands[idx] = demands[cluster_nodes].sum()
    
    # Map cluster IDs to their demands
    if len(unique_clusters) > 0:
        cluster_demand_map = torch.zeros(current_cluster_id, device=distance_matrix.device)
        for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
            if cluster_id >= 0:
                cluster_demand_map[cluster_id] = cluster_demands[idx]
        
        # Boost intra-cluster edges for reasonable demand clusters
        cluster_demand_i = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
        cluster_demand_j = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
        
        reasonable_demand_mask = (cluster_demand_i <= 2.0) & (cluster_demand_j <= 2.0)
        boost_mask = intra_cluster_mask & reasonable_demand_mask & knn_mask
        cluster_boost[boost_mask] = 0.15
        
        # Penalize inter-cluster edges connecting high-demand clusters
        inter_cluster_mask = (cluster_i != cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1) & (cluster_j != -1) & \
                             (cluster_i >= 0) & (cluster_j >= 0)
        high_demand_inter_mask = (cluster_demand_i > avg_demand) & (cluster_demand_j > avg_demand)
        penalty_mask = inter_cluster_mask & high_demand_inter_mask & knn_mask
        cluster_boost[penalty_mask] = -0.1
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + cluster_boost[knn_mask]
    
    # Asymmetric depot handling with demand/distance efficiency
    depot_idx = 0
    # Calculate efficiency of visiting each node after serving it (return to depot)
    depot_return_distances = distance_matrix[:, depot_idx]  # distances from all nodes to depot
    depot_return_distances[depot_idx] = torch.max(depot_return_distances)  # Avoid choosing depot to return to depot
    
    # Calculate efficiency as demand per unit distance to depot (higher is better for returning)
    depot_return_efficiency = demands / (depot_return_distances + 1e-8)  # Add small value to avoid division by zero
    # Scale and apply soft clipping to avoid extreme values
    depot_return_scaled = 0.12 * torch.tanh(depot_return_efficiency)
    
    # Calculate efficiency of starting from depot to each node
    depot_exit_distances = distance_matrix[depot_idx, :]  # distances from depot to all nodes
    depot_exit_efficiency = demands / (depot_exit_distances + 1e-8)  # Higher ratio means lower demand closer to depot
    # For exit, we want to encourage low-demand close nodes, so use the inverse concept but differently
    depot_exit_scaled = -0.08 * torch.tanh(depot_exit_efficiency)
    
    # Apply depot-specific adjustments
    # Depot return: encourage edges FROM nodes TO depot based on efficiency
    heuristic[:, depot_idx] = heuristic[:, depot_idx] + depot_return_scaled
    # Depot exit: encourage edges FROM depot TO nodes based on efficiency
    heuristic[depot_idx, :] = heuristic[depot_idx, :] + depot_exit_scaled
    
    # For non-knn edges, assign large negative values to discourage their selection
    non_knn_mask = ~knn_mask & ~mask
    heuristic[non_knn_mask] = -10.0
    
    # Additional capacity constraint: penalize edges that connect very high-demand nodes
    high_demand_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_threshold = avg_demand * 1.2
    
    high_demand_nodes = demands > high_demand_threshold
    high_demand_from = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(heuristic)
    high_demand_to = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(heuristic)
    
    high_demand_penalty[high_demand_from & high_demand_to] = -0.5
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Adjust based on dynamic k values - nodes with smaller neighborhoods get slightly higher incentives
    k_incentive = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    base_k_tensor = torch.tensor(base_k, dtype=torch.float, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].float()
        norm_k = k_i / base_k_tensor
        k_incentive[i, knn_mask[i]] = 0.05 * (1.0 - norm_k)
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + k_incentive[knn_mask]
    
    return heuristic

import torch
import math

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Implementation idea: Integrate spatial clustering information into edge scoring by detecting natural customer clusters
    (via DBSCAN-style clustering on coordinates derived from distance matrix) and boosting intra-cluster edges while 
    penalizing inter-cluster edges that don't align with capacity-feasible cluster sequencing. This addresses the 
    unresolved issue of incorporating spatial structure without disrupting existing heuristics, and complements 
    dynamic k-selection by adding a global geometric perspective to local neighborhood decisions. The implementation
    maintains the successful distance-based and capacity-aware components from parent solutions while adding
    spatial clustering awareness. Additionally, refine depot handling by implementing asymmetric depot-edge scoring
    based on demand/distance efficiency ratios.
    
    Implementation considerations: 
    - Use distance matrix to derive approximate coordinates via multidimensional scaling (MDS)
    - Apply DBSCAN-style clustering to detect customer groups
    - Boost intra-cluster edges and penalize inter-cluster edges that violate capacity constraints
    - Combine with dynamic k-nearest neighbor selection from parent solution
    - Maintain strong distance-based foundation while adding spatial clustering signals
    - Implement refined depot handling based on demand/distance efficiency
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: A tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all pairs of nodes
        demands: A tensor of shape (n,) representing demands for each node (normalized by vehicle capacity)
        
    Returns:
        A tensor of same shape as distance_matrix with heuristic values.
        Negative values indicate undesirable edges, positive values indicate promising ones.
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    
    # Early return for small matrices
    if n <= 1:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Extract coordinates using classical multidimensional scaling (MDS) approximation
    # Centering matrix H = I - 1/n * 11^T
    H = torch.eye(n, device=distance_matrix.device) - (1.0 / n) * torch.ones(n, n, device=distance_matrix.device)
    # Apply double centering to squared distance matrix
    D_squared = distance_matrix ** 2
    B = -0.5 * H @ D_squared @ H
    # Perform eigenvalue decomposition to get coordinates
    # Fixed: Replace deprecated torch.symeig with torch.linalg.eigh
    eigenvals, eigenvecs = torch.linalg.eigh(B)
    # Take top 2 dimensions (for 2D coordinates)
    idx = torch.argsort(eigenvals, descending=True)[:2]
    coords = eigenvecs[:, idx] * torch.sqrt(torch.abs(eigenvals[idx]))
    
    # Simplified clustering using distance-based approach instead of full DBSCAN
    # Determine epsilon as a fraction of average distance
    avg_dist = torch.mean(distance_matrix[distance_matrix > 0])  # exclude self-distances
    eps = avg_dist * 0.3  # use 30% of average distance as clustering radius
    
    # Assign cluster labels using a simplified approach
    cluster_labels = torch.full((n,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=distance_matrix.device)
    current_cluster_id = 0
    
    # Efficient clustering using distance matrix directly
    visited = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i]:
            continue
        
        # Find neighbors within eps distance (excluding self)
        neighbors = torch.where((distance_matrix[i] <= eps) & (distance_matrix[i] > 0))[0]
        
        if len(neighbors) > 0:  # If we have neighbors
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            cluster_labels[neighbors] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            visited[neighbors] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
        else:
            # Isolated point goes to its own cluster
            cluster_labels[i] = current_cluster_id
            visited[i] = True
            current_cluster_id += 1
    
    # Compute dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    sorted_dists, _ = torch.sort(distance_matrix, dim=1)
    
    k_max = min(n - 1, 20)
    k_min = 3
    
    avg_dists = []
    for i in range(k_min, k_max + 1):
        avg_dist = sorted_dists[:, 1:i+1].mean(dim=1)
        avg_dists.append(avg_dist.unsqueeze(0))
    
    avg_dists_tensor = torch.cat(avg_dists, dim=0).mean(dim=0)
    
    # Compute local demand density efficiently
    # Calculate average distance for each node to determine neighborhood size
    local_density = torch.zeros(n, device=distance_matrix.device)
    for i in range(n):
        radius = avg_dists_tensor[i]
        neighbors_mask = distance_matrix[i, :] <= radius
        local_density[i] = demands[neighbors_mask].sum()
    
    total_demand = demands[1:].sum()
    avg_demand = total_demand / (n - 1) if n > 1 else 1.0
    normalized_local_density = local_density / avg_demand
    
    # Determine dynamic k for each node based on local demand density
    base_k = max(5, int(n ** 0.5))
    density_factor = torch.clamp(2.0 / (1.0 + normalized_local_density), 0.5, 2.0)
    dynamic_k = torch.clamp((base_k * density_factor).int(), min=k_min, max=min(n-1, 15))
    
    # Create mask for k-nearest neighbors for each node (dynamic k) - vectorized
    mask = torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=distance_matrix.device)
    knn_mask = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix, dtype=torch.bool)
    
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].item()
        _, indices = torch.topk(distance_matrix[i], k=k_i+1, largest=False)
        # Remove self if present and take only k_i neighbors
        valid_indices = indices[indices != i][:k_i]
        knn_mask[i, valid_indices] = True
    
    # Initialize heuristic matrix
    heuristic = torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # For k-nearest neighbors, assign values based on distance and capacity considerations
    max_dist = torch.max(distance_matrix[knn_mask])
    max_dist = max_dist if max_dist > 0 else 1.0
    
    normalized_distances = distance_matrix / max_dist
    heuristic[knn_mask] = -0.75 * normalized_distances[knn_mask]  # Slightly reduced from -0.8 to allow more flexibility
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware component
    demand_i = demands.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    demand_j = demands.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    combined_demand_factor = (demand_i + demand_j) / (2 * avg_demand + 1e-8)
    capacity_adjustment = -0.05 * combined_demand_factor
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + capacity_adjustment[knn_mask]
    
    # Enhanced capacity-aware component: Consider individual demand ratios
    demand_ratio_i = demand_i / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    demand_ratio_j = demand_j / (avg_demand + 1e-8)
    
    high_demand_connection_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_both = (demand_ratio_i > 1.0) & (demand_ratio_j > 1.0)
    high_demand_connection_penalty[high_demand_both] = -0.05
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_connection_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Spatial clustering component - vectorized computation
    # Boost intra-cluster edges and penalize inter-cluster edges
    cluster_boost = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    
    # Vectorized cluster comparison
    cluster_i = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, n)
    cluster_j = cluster_labels.unsqueeze(0).expand(n, -1)
    
    # Identify intra-cluster edges
    intra_cluster_mask = (cluster_i == cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1)
    
    # Calculate cluster demands efficiently
    unique_clusters = torch.unique(cluster_labels)
    cluster_demands = torch.zeros(len(unique_clusters), device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        cluster_nodes = torch.where(cluster_labels == cluster_id)[0]
        cluster_demands[idx] = demands[cluster_nodes].sum()
    
    # Map cluster IDs to their demands
    cluster_demand_map = torch.zeros(current_cluster_id, device=distance_matrix.device)
    for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(unique_clusters):
        if cluster_id >= 0:
            cluster_demand_map[cluster_id] = cluster_demands[idx]
    
    # Boost intra-cluster edges for clusters with reasonable demand
    cluster_demand_i = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
    cluster_demand_j = cluster_demand_map[cluster_labels]
    
    # Boost intra-cluster edges for reasonable demand clusters
    reasonable_demand_mask = (cluster_demand_i <= 2.0) & (cluster_demand_j <= 2.0)
    boost_mask = intra_cluster_mask & reasonable_demand_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[boost_mask] = 0.15
    
    # Penalize inter-cluster edges connecting high-demand clusters
    inter_cluster_mask = (cluster_i != cluster_j) & (cluster_i != -1) & (cluster_j != -1)
    high_demand_inter_mask = (cluster_demand_i > avg_demand) & (cluster_demand_j > avg_demand)
    penalty_mask = inter_cluster_mask & high_demand_inter_mask & knn_mask
    cluster_boost[penalty_mask] = -0.1
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + cluster_boost[knn_mask]
    
    # Refined depot handling with demand/distance efficiency
    depot_idx = 0
    # Calculate efficiency of visiting each node after serving it (return to depot)
    # Higher demand with shorter distance to depot should have higher incentive to return
    depot_return_distances = distance_matrix[:, depot_idx]  # distances from all nodes to depot
    depot_return_distances[depot_idx] = torch.max(depot_return_distances)  # Avoid choosing depot to return to depot
    
    # Calculate efficiency as demand per unit distance to depot (higher is better for returning)
    depot_return_efficiency = demands / (depot_return_distances + 1e-8)  # Add small value to avoid division by zero
    # Scale and apply soft clipping to avoid extreme values
    depot_return_scaled = 0.12 * torch.tanh(depot_return_efficiency)
    
    # Calculate efficiency of starting from depot to each node
    # Lower demand with shorter distance from depot should have higher incentive to start
    depot_exit_distances = distance_matrix[depot_idx, :]  # distances from depot to all nodes
    depot_exit_efficiency = demands / (depot_exit_distances + 1e-8)  # Higher ratio means lower demand closer to depot
    # For exit, we want to encourage low-demand close nodes, so use the inverse concept but differently
    depot_exit_scaled = -0.08 * torch.tanh(depot_exit_efficiency)
    
    # Apply depot-specific adjustments
    # Depot return: encourage edges FROM nodes TO depot based on efficiency
    heuristic[:, depot_idx] = heuristic[:, depot_idx] + depot_return_scaled
    # Depot exit: encourage edges FROM depot TO nodes based on efficiency
    heuristic[depot_idx, :] = heuristic[depot_idx, :] + depot_exit_scaled
    
    # For non-knn edges, assign large negative values to discourage their selection
    non_knn_mask = ~knn_mask & ~mask
    heuristic[non_knn_mask] = -10.0
    
    # Additional capacity constraint: penalize edges that connect high-demand nodes
    high_demand_penalty = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    high_demand_threshold = avg_demand * 1.2
    
    high_demand_nodes = demands > high_demand_threshold
    high_demand_from = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(1).expand_as(heuristic)
    high_demand_to = high_demand_nodes.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(heuristic)
    
    high_demand_penalty[high_demand_from & high_demand_to] = -0.5
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + high_demand_penalty[knn_mask]
    
    # Adjust based on dynamic k values - nodes with smaller neighborhoods get slightly higher incentives
    k_incentive = torch.zeros_like(heuristic)
    base_k_tensor = torch.tensor(base_k, dtype=torch.float, device=distance_matrix.device)
    
    for i in range(n):
        k_i = dynamic_k[i].float()
        norm_k = k_i / base_k_tensor
        k_incentive[i, knn_mask[i]] = 0.05 * (1.0 - norm_k)
    
    heuristic[knn_mask] = heuristic[knn_mask] + k_incentive[knn_mask]
    
    return heuristic
